frequency_question: How often do jurisdictions with a CCyB framework raise the buffer rate above 0% during a standard economic expansion phase lasting up to 3 years?
membership_rule: Members are G20 or Basel Committee member jurisdictions that formally adopted the Basel III CCyB framework and maintained it through at least one full economic cycle. Excluded are jurisdictions without an active macroprudential authority or where the framework was not operational.
window: A rolling 3-year observation window corresponding to the maximum time horizon of the specific question.
coverage_note: 10 named cases covering major jurisdictions; believed to represent the primary applicable population of advanced economy cycles under Basel III.
known_gaps: Varying definitions of credit-to-GDP gaps across jurisdictions leading to heterogeneous activation thresholds.
skeleton: 10 distinct jurisdiction-cycle observations across major developed economies implementing the Basel III framework.
multiplier: 10 observed cycles, 6 positive activations, yielding a 60 percent base rate for peer jurisdictions, adjusted downward for the US historical institutional reluctance to activate above 0%.
validity_reason: Macroprudential frameworks and Basel III rules evolve slowly over multi-year regulatory regimes.
